title: Properness tested on local rings of normal finite-type curves
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact $k$-morphism. Then $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] if and only if the following condition holds. Let $C$ be any integral scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] whose local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $c\in C$ be a closed point with $\dim\mathcal O_{C,c}=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and put $U=C\setminus\{c\}$, $R=\mathcal O_{C,c}$ and $F=\operatorname{Frac}R$. For every pair of $k$-morphisms $u:U\to X$ and $v:C\to Y$ with $fu=v|_U$, there is a unique $k$-morphism $h:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ such that $fh$ is the restriction of $v$ to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $h|_{\operatorname{Spec}F}$ is the restriction of $u$. Here a local ring is the structure-sheaf stalk, and $F$ is the field of fractions, whose elements are quotients of elements of the domain $R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. No reducedness hypothesis is imposed on $X$ or $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0GWX, limits-lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-proper, specialized to S=Spec k (a field is Nagata); the condition uses precisely the C,U,c diagrams and their local DVR squares, not arbitrary fraction-field maps.

proof.text: Write $p_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $p_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the structure maps. Since $p_Yf=p_X$ is locally of finite type, clause (a) of [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target] gives that $f$ is locally of finite type. Together with its assumed quasi-compactness this makes $f$ finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The only ideals of the field $k$ are $0,k$, so $k$ is Noetherian and its single affine spectrum is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to $p_X$ to obtain that $X$ is locally Noetherian. The same argument applies to every finite-type test scheme $C$ in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0GWX (lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-proper), finite-type hypothesis; morphisms.tex Tags 01T8 (lemma-permanence-finite-type) and 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian).

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is proper and fix a test diagram $C,c,U,u,v$. The scheme $C$ is locally Noetherian by step 1. Choose a Noetherian affine chart $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $c$, using [pqf-def-locnoeth]. The local ring $R=\mathcal O_{C,c}$ is $A_{\mathfrak p_c}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. It is a normal local domain of dimension one by the hypotheses, so [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes $R$ a discrete valuation ring, in particular a valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Properness includes separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension] applied to the generic restriction of $u$ over $v|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$ supplies exactly one $h$ as required. This lift is a $k$-morphism because $fh=v|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$ and $f,v$ are $k$-morphisms.

source.place: Tag 0GWX (lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-proper), implication (1) to (2), and its DVR footnote; algebra.tex Tags 00FN and 00PD.

proof.text: Conversely assume the unique-lift condition of the item. Forgetting uniqueness gives condition (3) of [lem-sfb-normal-curve-universal-closedness-test] for $g=f$: its $C,c,U,R,F$ and its two given maps are exactly those of the item, rather than arbitrary maps out of fraction fields. That node's implication (3) to (1) shows that $f$ is universally closed.

Put $P=X\times_YX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $\delta:X\to P$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The projection $p_1$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change] applied to $f$; composing it with $p_X$ shows that $P$ is locally of finite type over $k$ by clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Since $p_1\delta=\mathrm{id}_X$, clause (a) of [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target] gives that $\delta$ is locally of finite type. It is also quasi-compact: by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], intersections of affine opens of $X$ are quasi-compact. Cover $Y$ by affine opens $V$, and $f^{-1}(V)$ by affine opens $A,B$. The products $A\times_VB$ cover $P$ by affine opens, by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]; their inclusions are open since on a scheme test the map factors through the product precisely when its two components factor through $A,B$. The inverse image of $A\times_VB$ under $\delta$ is $A\cap B$, hence quasi-compact. For any map from a quasi-compact scheme to an affine scheme, take a finite affine cover of its source. Inverse images of basic opens are finite unions of principal opens by [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-pullback], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Every affine open of the target has a finite basic-open cover by the same two nodes. Thus each restricted map $A\cap B\to A\times_VB$ is quasi-compact. Now [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] gives that $\delta$ is quasi-compact, hence finite type. Finally $\delta$ is a monomorphism: if $\delta r=\delta s$, compose with $p_1$ to get $r=s$.

source.place: Tag 0GWW (lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-separation), proof, quasi-compactness of the diagonal; morphisms.tex Tags 01T3, 01T4, 01T8 and properties.tex Tag 01OY.

proof.text: Verify condition (3) of [lem-sfb-normal-curve-universal-closedness-test] for $\delta$. Take a test diagram $a:U\to X$ and $b:C\to P$ with $\delta a=b|_U$, and write $b_i=p_i b$. The fibre-product identities [def-pc-fibre-product] give $fb_1=fb_2=:v$ and $b_1|_U=b_2|_U=a$. The restrictions $b_1|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$ and $b_2|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$ are therefore two lifts for the original condition applied to $(a,v)$. Uniqueness makes them equal. Set $h=b_1|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$. Both projections of $\delta h$ agree with those of $b|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$, so the fibre-product universal property gives $\delta h=b|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$. Its generic restriction is $a|_{\operatorname{Spec}F}$. Thus the diagonal satisfies the existence test, and that node makes $\delta$ universally closed. Step 4 verified its quasi-compactness and both schemes' local finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0GWW (lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-separation), diagonal argument, using the local form of uniqueness directly; Tag 0GWV for the diagonal.

proof.text: The monomorphism $\delta$ is separated by [lem-trf-scheme-monomorphism-separated]. It is finite type by step 4 and universally closed by step 5, hence proper by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] to conclude that $\delta$ is a closed immersion. Therefore $f$ is separated. Combining this with finite type from step 1 and universal closedness from step 3, the same definition makes $f$ proper. No step replaced $X$ or $Y$ by a reduction.

source.place: Tag 0GWX (lemma-essentially-finite-type-criterion-proper), final assembly; schemes.tex Tag 01L4 (lemma-monomorphism-separated), etale.tex Tag 04XV (lemma-characterize-closed-immersion).

lean.statement: theorem isProper_iff_normal_curve_local_test (k : Type u) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (p : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (q : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType p] [LocallyOfFiniteType q] (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] (hf : f ≫ q = p) : IsProper f ↔ ∀ (C : Scheme.{u}) (s : C ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) [IsIntegral C] [LocallyOfFiniteType s] [QuasiCompact s], (∀ z : C, IsDomain (C.presheaf.stalk z) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (C.presheaf.stalk z)) → ∀ (c : C), IsClosed ({c} : Set C) → ringKrullDim (C.presheaf.stalk c) = 1 → ∀ (U : C.Opens), (U : Set C) = {c}ᶜ → ∀ (a : U.toScheme ⟶ X) (b : C ⟶ Y), a ≫ p = U.ι ≫ s → b ≫ q = s → a ≫ f = U.ι ≫ b → ∃! h : Spec (C.presheaf.stalk c) ⟶ X, h ≫ p = C.fromSpecStalk c ≫ s ∧ h ≫ f = C.fromSpecStalk c ≫ b ∧ pullback.snd U.ι (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk c) (FractionRing (C.presheaf.stalk c)))) ≫ C.fromSpecStalk c) ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk c) (FractionRing (C.presheaf.stalk c)))) ≫ h = pullback.fst U.ι (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (C.presheaf.stalk c) (FractionRing (C.presheaf.stalk c)))) ≫ C.fromSpecStalk c) ≫ a
